root_idea.summary: The root denotes placing a separation between two things, thereby preventing contact, movement, or action between them.
root_idea.development: From interposing and holding apart, the lexical family develops meanings of barriers, restraint, mutual abstention, protective separation, waist-fastening, and related forms of attachment. The regional name al-Ḥijāz is likewise explained through its separating position.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form حَاجِزٌ.
The Quranic plural active participle حَاجِزِينَ belongs to the same lexical item as حَاجِزٌ and is displayed under its singular citation form.

senses.definition: A barrier or separating partition between two things.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, used for the separator placed between two bodies of water in the expression وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا.

senses.definition: One who prevents, restrains, or wards off.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural active participle حَاجِزِينَ describes those who could prevent it; in 69:47 it qualifies أَحَدٌ, which is grammatically singular but construed in the plural sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a figurative idiom, a person's condition or standing cannot be concealed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic tropical usage, not the ordinary concrete sense of preventing or separating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fence or partition something with a wall or other barrier.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the passive construction of a roof that has not been fenced around with a wall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reciprocal prevention of fighting; mutual abstention from combat and the making of peace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of opposing parties or troops, especially in the conventional contrast between محاجزة and مناجزة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate or part from one another; to mutually withhold, forsake, or relinquish one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people or groups; in an imperative expression it can mean “separate the people” or “withhold yourself.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take hold of one another by the waistbands; figuratively, to seek aid, refuge, or protection from one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived reciprocal construction connected with حُجْزَةٌ, the waistband or grasping place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be restrained or held back; to restrain oneself, refrain, forbear, or abstain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive or reflexive realization of the basic preventing sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave, forsake, or relinquish something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْهُ in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To defend oneself or protect oneself by means of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction احتجز به takes the protecting means with بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To carry something in the waistband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete clothing-related use of the derived verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tie or wrap an izār around the waist, bringing its ends together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِإِزَارِهِ for fastening or wrapping the waist garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be encompassed or bounded by surrounding terrain or other boundaries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of a place surrounded by stony tracts and mountains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to the province of al-Ḥijāz.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized geographic usage of the derived verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who abstains from what is unlawful or indecorous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related expression طَيِّبُ الحُجْزَةِ carries the same moral characterization, especially concerning sexual propriety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A severe year that confines people to their tents or houses and forces them to slaughter valuable camels for food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical usage attested in poetic evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of an izār where it is folded or tied around the waist; by extension, the waist garment itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of the corresponding upper fold or waistband of trousers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Patience, endurance, or hardiness in difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom derived from the firmness of a waistband or fastening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Full or protuberant in the flanks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative bodily description; the condition is presented as a fault in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means of seeking another's aid, refuge, or protection by taking hold of the person's waistband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used figuratively of laying hold of a means of access or nearness to God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figurative attachment or ordered linkage: words may be connected in sequence, and persons or kin may be described as attached to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in idioms about coherent speech and the attachment of kin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode, manner, or form of tying an izār.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A clothing term distinct from the place or part where the garment is tied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope fastened from a camel's hip to its pastern.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete nominal usage from which a related sense of joining or gathering is conceived.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or group who prevents someone from obtaining a right; alternatively, defenders who mediate between people and decide disputes justly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized social and legal usage with two reported interpretations; it is distinct from the general Quranic sense of a preventer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hit or hurt at the part of the body where the izār is tied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial bodily description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bodily place or part where the izār is tied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the waist-fastening location, not the act of fastening itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the waist bound with an izār.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is also used of a woman whose garment is tied over the awrah.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The barrier sense is represented; the regional-name explanation is etymological context.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence حَاجِزِينَ is a plural active participle used in the construction وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِجَبَّارٍ وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِجَبَّارٍ? No modern location has been inferred from Lane citation notation; the supplied QAC locations alone are used for Quran examples.
